basis: Comedocarcinoma is classically mammary; breast has no axis. The supplied site-unspecified histologic definition establishes no covered organ.
Disease of cutaneous appendages, including hair, nails and skin glands; subtype-specific organs are not generalized.
Neoplasm located in the temporal lobe of the brain.
Osteosclerosis and fractures define this skeletal disease; anemia and neurologic abnormalities occur in 5-29%, visual impairment in 1-4%.
Chronic autoinflammatory sterile osteitis and hyperostosis of the sternocostoclavicular region; associated pustulosis is not established in at least 30%.
Autoimmune cutaneous disease causing scarring and pigment loss; systemic lupus is a separate diagnosis, and arthralgia does not establish joint damage.
Squamous carcinoma arising in ovarian epithelium; reproductive origin without a defining endocrine disorder.
Familial febrile seizure disorder; all reported patients have seizures, establishing neurologic dysfunction.
Dystonia and tremor define a neurologic movement disorder; compensatory muscle hypertrophy is not muscle damage, and arrhythmias are occasional.
Proliferation of steroidogenic luteinized ovarian stromal cells represents a gonadal endocrine lesion; no additional organ damage is established.
Cancer originates in the sphenoidal sinus; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Purine nucleotide metabolism enzyme deficiency causing skeletal myopathy; weakness and atrophy establish muscle involvement, without independent nerve disease.
Adenocarcinoma of the reproductive tract's Bartholin gland; this vestibular gland is outside the covered axes.
Urinary bladder disease belongs to the renal axis; infectious and neurologic mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly and developmental delays; no independent systemic metabolic phenotype is established.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 2/2 patients; secondary respiratory infections do not establish primary immunodeficiency.
Congenital anomalous systemic venous drainage causes a right-to-left shunt; hypoxemia is not lung damage, and brain abscess is a minority complication.
Permanent neonatal diabetes; direct KCNJ11-related neurodevelopmental dysfunction occurs in 4/13 patients (~31%); contractures and ptosis each occur in 3/13.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: skin is the origin, malignant lymphocytes establish the blood-cell axis, and lymphoma requires the immune axis.
Congenital abducens dysinnervation defines ocular motility dysfunction; supplied HPO lists sensorineural hearing loss and vertebral fusion each as frequent (30-79%).
Frontonasal arterial-venous malformation; skin damage, visual impairment and heart failure are possible but not established in at least 30%.
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma originating in the lung or bronchus.
Neoplasms of histiocytic and dendritic hematopoietic cells; this group is not inherently lymphoma, and no additional organ is consistently affected.
Glycosylation defect with cerebellar disease; strabismus 80-99%, hepatic disease ~60% with fibrosis reported; renal cysts 69%, bone disease and coagulopathy omitted at cap.
Coxiella infection; pneumonia and liver abnormalities are listed at 5-29%. Enzyme elevation, reactive splenomegaly and transient rash alone do not establish organ damage.
